name: Google Sheets
description: Google Sheets is a cloud-based spreadsheet tool enabling real-time collaboration, data analysis, and integration with other Google Workspace apps

tools.name: Add Sheet to Existing Spreadsheet
tools.description: Add a GRID sheet with rows and columns to an existing spreadsheet. This action does not create chart-only or DATA_SOURCE sheets. Use properties to configure the GRID sheet's dimensions, tab color, position, visibility, and text direction. Notes: - Sheet names must be unique; use forceUnique=true to auto-append suffix (_2, _3) if name exists - For tab colors, use EITHER rgbColor OR themeColor, not both - Avoid 'index' when creating sheets in parallel (causes errors)

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: The name for the new sheet tab. Must be unique within the spreadsheet. Example: "Q3 Report", "Sales Data 2025". This is a convenience parameter - alternatively, you can set this via properties.title. Note: sheet_name is also accepted as an alias for title.

inputs.name: properties
inputs.about: Advanced GRID sheet properties such as dimensions, tab color, position, visibility, and text direction. For simple cases, use the title parameter directly.

inputs.name: force_unique
inputs.about: When True (default), automatically ensures the sheet name is unique by appending a numeric suffix (e.g., '_2', '_3') if the requested name already exists. This makes the action resilient to retries and parallel workflows. When False, the action fails with an error if a sheet with the same name alrea

inputs.name: spreadsheet_id
inputs.about: REQUIRED. Cannot be empty. The ID of the target spreadsheet where the new sheet will be added. This is the long alphanumeric string in the Google Sheet URL (e.g., '1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgvE2upms'). Use 'Search Spreadsheets' action to find the spreadsheet ID by name if you don't have it

tools.name: Aggregate Column Data
tools.description: Aggregates data from a column in a Google Sheet, either across all rows or rows matching column-value filters. Supports sum, average, count, minimum, maximum, and percentage.

inputs.name: operation
inputs.about: The mathematical operation to perform on the target column values.

inputs.name: sheet_name
inputs.about: The name of the specific sheet within the spreadsheet. Matching is case-insensitive. If no exact match is found, partial matches will be attempted (e.g., 'overview' will match 'Overview 2025').

inputs.name: search_value
inputs.about: The exact value to search for in the search column. Case-sensitive by default. If not provided (or if search_column is not provided), all rows in the target column will be aggregated without filtering.

inputs.name: search_column
inputs.about: The column to search in for filtering rows. Can be a letter (e.g., 'A', 'B') or column name from header row (e.g., 'Region', 'Department'). If not provided, all rows in the target column will be aggregated without filtering.

inputs.name: target_column
inputs.about: The column to aggregate data from. Can be a letter (e.g., 'C', 'D') or column name from header row (e.g., 'Sales', 'Revenue').

inputs.name: case_sensitive
inputs.about: Whether the search should be case-sensitive.

inputs.name: has_header_row
inputs.about: Whether the first row contains column headers. If True, column names can be used for search_column and target_column.

inputs.name: spreadsheet_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the Google Sheets spreadsheet.

inputs.name: percentage_total
inputs.about: For percentage operation, the total value to calculate percentage against. If not provided, uses sum of all values in target column.

inputs.name: additional_filters
inputs.about: Extra column=value conditions applied with AND logic on top of search_column/search_value. Use this to filter on multiple columns simultaneously. Example: [{"column": "Region", "value": "APAC"}] combined with search_column=Product/search_value=Beacon returns only rows where Product=Beacon AND Region

tools.name: Append Dimension
tools.description: Tool to append new rows or columns to a sheet, increasing its size. Use when you need to add empty rows or columns to an existing sheet.

inputs.name: length
inputs.about: The number of rows or columns to append.

inputs.name: sheet_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the sheet (not the sheet name). This is a non-negative integer found in the sheet's URL as the 'gid' parameter (e.g., gid=0) or in the sheet properties. The first sheet in a spreadsheet typically has sheet_id=0.

inputs.name: dimension
inputs.about: Specifies whether to append rows or columns.

inputs.name: spreadsheet_id
inputs.about: The ID of the spreadsheet.

inputs.name: response_ranges
inputs.about: Limits the ranges of the spreadsheet to include in the response.

inputs.name: response_include_grid_data
inputs.about: True if grid data should be included in the response (if includeSpreadsheetInResponse is true).

inputs.name: include_spreadsheet_in_response
inputs.about: True if the updated spreadsheet should be included in the response.

tools.name: Auto-Resize Rows or Columns
tools.description: Auto-fit column widths or row heights for a dimension range using batchUpdate.autoResizeDimensions. Use when you need to automatically adjust row heights or column widths to fit content after writing data.

inputs.name: sheet_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the sheet to resize. Either sheet_id or sheet_name must be provided. If both are provided, sheet_name takes precedence and will be resolved to sheet_id.

inputs.name: dimension
inputs.about: The dimension to auto-resize. Use 'ROWS' to auto-fit row heights or 'COLUMNS' to auto-fit column widths.

inputs.name: end_index
inputs.about: The zero-based end index of the dimension range to resize (exclusive). Must be greater than start_index. For example, to resize columns A-C, use start_index=0 and end_index=3.

inputs.name: sheet_name
inputs.about: The name of the sheet to resize. Either sheet_id or sheet_name must be provided. Using sheet_name is recommended as it's more intuitive. If both sheet_id and sheet_name are provided, sheet_name takes precedence.

inputs.name: start_index
inputs.about: The zero-based start index of the dimension range to resize (inclusive). For columns, 0 = column A. For rows, 0 = row 1.

inputs.name: spreadsheet_id
inputs.about: The ID of the spreadsheet containing the sheet to resize.

tools.name: Batch Clear Values By Data Filter
tools.description: Clears one or more ranges of values from a spreadsheet using data filters. The caller must specify the spreadsheet ID and one or more DataFilters. Ranges matching any of the specified data filters will be cleared. Only values are cleared -- all other properties of the cell (such as formatting, data validation, etc..) are kept.

inputs.name: dataFilters
inputs.about: The DataFilters used to determine which ranges to clear.

inputs.name: spreadsheetId
inputs.about: The ID of the spreadsheet to update.

tools.name: Batch get spreadsheet
tools.description: Retrieves values from specified cell ranges in a Google Spreadsheet. If ranges are omitted or empty after filtering blank entries, it retrieves data from the first sheet.

inputs.name: ranges
inputs.about: A list of cell ranges in A1 notation from which to retrieve data. If this list is omitted, empty, or contains only empty strings, all data from the first sheet of the spreadsheet will be fetched. Empty strings in the list are automatically filtered out. Supported formats: (1) Bare sheet name like 'S

inputs.name: majorDimension
inputs.about: The major dimension for organizing data in results.

inputs.name: spreadsheet_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the Google Spreadsheet from which data will be retrieved. This is the ID found in the spreadsheet URL after /d/. You can provide either the spreadsheet ID directly or a full Google Sheets URL (the ID will be extracted automatically).

inputs.name: valueRenderOption
inputs.about: How values should be rendered in the output. FORMATTED_VALUE: Values are calculated and formatted (default). UNFORMATTED_VALUE: Values are calculated but not formatted. FORMULA: Values are not calculated; the formula is returned instead.

inputs.name: dateTimeRenderOption
inputs.about: How dates and times should be rendered in the output. SERIAL_NUMBER: Dates are returned as serial numbers (default). FORMATTED_STRING: Dates returned as formatted strings.

inputs.name: empty_strings_filtered
inputs.about: Indicates whether empty strings were filtered from the response.

tools.name: Batch update spreadsheet (Deprecated)
tools.description: Deprecated: Writes values to one range in a Google Sheet, or appends rows when no start cell is given. It may expand the sheet grid; if a recognized default sheet name is not found, it uses the first sheet instead.

inputs.name: values
inputs.about: A 2D array of cell values where each inner array represents a row. Values can be strings, numbers, booleans, or None/null for empty cells. Ensure columns are properly aligned across rows.

inputs.name: sheet_name
inputs.about: The name of the specific sheet (tab) within the spreadsheet to update (required, separate from cell reference). Case-insensitive matching is supported (e.g., 'sheet1' will match 'Sheet1'). Note: Default sheet names are locale-dependent (e.g., 'Sheet1' in English, 'Foglio1' in Italian, 'Hoja 1' in Sp

inputs.name: spreadsheet_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the Google Sheets spreadsheet to be updated. Must be an alphanumeric string (with hyphens and underscores allowed) typically 44 characters long. Can be found in the spreadsheet URL between '/d/' and '/edit'. Example: 'https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKv

inputs.name: value_input_option
inputs.about: How input data should be interpreted. 'USER_ENTERED': Values are parsed as if typed by a user (e.g., strings may become numbers/dates, formulas are calculated). 'RAW': Values are stored exactly as provided without parsing (e.g., '123' stays as string, '=SUM(A1:B1)' is not calculated).

inputs.name: first_cell_location
inputs.about: The starting cell for the update range, specified as a single cell in A1 notation WITHOUT sheet prefix (e.g., 'A1', 'B2', 'AA931'). The update will extend from this cell to the right and down based on the provided values. Sheet name must be provided separately in the 'sheet_name' field. If omitted o

inputs.name: include_values_in_response
inputs.about: If set to True, the response will include the updated values in the 'spreadsheet.responses[].updatedData' field. The updatedData object contains 'range' (A1 notation), 'majorDimension' (ROWS), and 'values' (2D array of the actual cell values after the update).

tools.name: Batch Update Values by Data Filter
tools.description: Tool to update values in ranges matching data filters. Use when you need to update specific data in a Google Sheet based on criteria rather than fixed cell ranges.

inputs.name: data
inputs.about: The new values to apply to the spreadsheet. If more than one range is matched by the specified DataFilter the specified values are applied to all of those ranges. Can be provided as a JSON string or as a list of DataFilterValueRange objects.

inputs.name: spreadsheetId
inputs.about: The ID of the spreadsheet to update.

inputs.name: valueInputOption
inputs.about: How the input data should be interpreted. RAW: Values are stored exactly as entered, without parsing. USER_ENTERED: Values are parsed as if typed by a user (numbers stay numbers, strings prefixed with '=' become formulas, etc.). INPUT_VALUE_OPTION_UNSPECIFIED: Default input value option is not speci

inputs.name: includeValuesInResponse
inputs.about: Determines if the update response should include the values of the cells that were updated. By default, responses do not include the updated values.

inputs.name: responseValueRenderOption
inputs.about: Determines how values in the response should be rendered. The default render option is FORMATTED_VALUE.

inputs.name: responseDateTimeRenderOption
inputs.about: Determines how dates, times, and durations in the response should be rendered. This is ignored if responseValueRenderOption is FORMATTED_VALUE. The default dateTime render option is SERIAL_NUMBER.

tools.name: Clear Basic Filter
tools.description: Tool to clear the basic filter from a sheet. Use when you need to remove an existing basic filter from a specific sheet within a Google Spreadsheet.

inputs.name: sheet_id
inputs.about: The ID of the sheet on which the basic filter should be cleared.

inputs.name: spreadsheet_id
inputs.about: The ID of the spreadsheet.

inputs.name: response_ranges
inputs.about: Limits the ranges included in the response spreadsheet. Only applicable when include_spreadsheet_in_response is true.

inputs.name: response_include_grid_data
inputs.about: True if grid data should be returned in the response. Only applicable when include_spreadsheet_in_response is true.

inputs.name: include_spreadsheet_in_response
inputs.about: Determines if the update response should include the spreadsheet resource.

tools.name: Clear spreadsheet values
tools.description: Clears cell content (preserving formatting and notes) from a specified A1 notation range in a Google Spreadsheet; the range must correspond to an existing sheet and cells.

inputs.name: range
inputs.about: The A1 notation of the range to clear values from (e.g., 'Sheet1!A1:B2', 'MySheet!C:C', or 'A1:D5'). If the sheet name is omitted (e.g., 'A1:B2'), the operation applies to the first visible sheet.

inputs.name: spreadsheet_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the Google Spreadsheet from which to clear values. This ID can be found in the URL of the spreadsheet.

tools.name: Create Chart in Google Sheets
tools.description: Create a chart in a Google Sheets spreadsheet using a specified data range and chart type, or an optional full chart specification. The chart type and data range are required even when supplying a chart specification.

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: Optional title for the chart.

inputs.name: sheet_id
inputs.about: The numeric sheetId (not the sheet name/title) of the worksheet where the chart will be created. This is a unique integer identifier for the sheet within the spreadsheet. inputs.name: subtitle
inputs.about: Optional subtitle for the chart.

inputs.name: chart_spec

inputs.name: data_range
inputs.about: A single contiguous range of data for the chart in A1 notation (e.g., 'A1:C10' or 'Sheet1!B2:D20'). Must be a single continuous range - comma-separated multi-ranges (e.g., 'A1:A10,C1:C10') are not supported. inputs.name: x_axis_title
inputs.about: Optional title for the X-axis.

inputs.name: y_axis_title
inputs.about: Optional title for the Y-axis.

inputs.name: background_red
inputs.about: Red component of chart background color (0.0-1.0). If not specified, uses default.

inputs.name: spreadsheet_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the Google Sheets spreadsheet where the chart will be created. Must be the actual spreadsheet ID from the URL (e.g., '1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgvE2upms'), NOT the spreadsheet name or title. Find it in the URL: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/SPREADSHEET_ID/

inputs.name: background_blue
inputs.about: Blue component of chart background color (0.0-1.0). If not specified, uses default.

inputs.name: legend_position
inputs.about: Position of the chart legend. Options: BOTTOM_LEGEND, TOP_LEGEND, LEFT_LEGEND, RIGHT_LEGEND, NO_LEGEND.

inputs.name: background_green
inputs.about: Green component of chart background color (0.0-1.0). If not specified, uses default.

tools.name: Create a Google Sheet
tools.description: Creates a new Google Spreadsheet in Drive with an optional title and folder ID or exact folder name. Multiple matching folders return choices before creation; if moving a created spreadsheet to the requested folder fails, the response reports partial success.

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: The title for the new Google Sheet. If omitted, Google will create a spreadsheet with a default name like 'Untitled spreadsheet'.

inputs.name: folder_id
inputs.about: Google Drive folder ID where the spreadsheet should be created. If provided, the spreadsheet will be moved to this folder after creation. Takes precedence over folder_name.

inputs.name: folder_name
inputs.about: Google Drive folder name where the spreadsheet should be created. If provided and folder_id is not provided, the action will search for a folder with this exact name. If multiple folders match, you'll receive a list to choose from. If no folder matches, an error is returned.

tools.name: Create spreadsheet column
tools.description: Inserts a new column in a Google Spreadsheet at a specified index. Select the target sheet by numeric ID or name; if neither is provided, sheet ID 0 is used.

inputs.name: sheet_id
inputs.about: The numeric identifier of the specific sheet (tab) within the spreadsheet. Defaults to 0 (the first sheet) if neither sheet_id nor sheet_name is provided. Use GOOGLESHEETS_GET_SHEET_NAMES or GOOGLESHEETS_FIND_WORKSHEET_BY_TITLE to obtain the sheet_id from a sheet name.

inputs.name: sheet_name
inputs.about: The name (title) of the sheet/tab where the column will be added. If provided, the action will look up the sheet_id automatically. If both sheet_id and sheet_name are provided, sheet_id takes precedence.

inputs.name: insert_index
inputs.about: The 0-based index at which the new column will be inserted. For example, an index of 0 inserts the column before the current first column (A), and an index of 1 inserts it between the current columns A and B.

inputs.name: spreadsheet_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the Google Spreadsheet where the column will be created.

inputs.name: response_ranges
inputs.about: Limits the ranges of the spreadsheet to include in the response. Only used if includeSpreadsheetInResponse is true.

inputs.name: inherit_from_before
inputs.about: If true, the new column inherits properties (e.g., formatting, width) from the column immediately to its left (the preceding column). If false (default), it inherits from the column immediately to its right (the succeeding column). This is ignored if there is no respective preceding or succeeding co

inputs.name: response_include_grid_data
inputs.about: If true, grid data will be included in the response (only used if includeSpreadsheetInResponse is true).

inputs.name: include_spreadsheet_in_response
inputs.about: If true, the updated spreadsheet will be included in the response. Defaults to true if not specified.

tools.name: Create spreadsheet row
tools.description: Inserts a new, empty row into a specified sheet of a Google Spreadsheet at a given index, optionally inheriting formatting from the row above.

inputs.name: sheet_id
inputs.about: The numeric identifier of the sheet (tab) within the spreadsheet where the row will be inserted. This ID (gid) is found in the URL of the spreadsheet (e.g., '0' for the first sheet). Either sheet_id or sheet_name must be provided.

inputs.name: sheet_name
inputs.about: The human-readable name of the sheet (tab) within the spreadsheet where the row will be inserted (e.g., 'Sheet1'). Either sheet_id or sheet_name must be provided. If both are provided, sheet_id takes precedence.

inputs.name: insert_index
inputs.about: The 0-based index at which the new row should be inserted. For example, an index of 0 inserts the row at the beginning of the sheet. If the index is greater than the current number of rows, the row is appended.

inputs.name: spreadsheet_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the Google Spreadsheet. Can be provided as the ID (e.g., '1qpyC0XzHc_-_d824s2VfopkHh7D0jW4aXCS1D_AlGA') or as a full URL (the ID will be extracted automatically).

inputs.name: response_ranges
inputs.about: Limits the ranges included in the response spreadsheet. Only meaningful when include_spreadsheet_in_response is True. Use A1 notation (e.g., ['Sheet1!A1:D10']).

inputs.name: inherit_from_before
inputs.about: If True, the newly inserted row will inherit formatting and properties from the row immediately preceding its insertion point. If False, it will have default formatting.

inputs.name: response_include_grid_data
inputs.about: If True, grid data will be included in the response spreadsheet. Only meaningful when include_spreadsheet_in_response is True. Default is False.

inputs.name: include_spreadsheet_in_response
inputs.about: If True, the response will include the full updated Spreadsheet resource. Default behavior includes the spreadsheet when this parameter is not specified.

This action is irreversible — once a chart is deleted, it cannot be recovered. The chart data source (the cells containing the data) remains unchanged; only the chart visualization is removed.

inputs.name: chart_id
inputs.about: The unique numeric identifier of the chart to delete (also known as objectId or chartId). This is the chart's ID within the spreadsheet, not the sheet ID. You can retrieve chart IDs using the 'Get Spreadsheet Info' action - look for sheets[].charts[].chartId in the response. Each chart has a unique

inputs.name: spreadsheet_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the Google Sheets spreadsheet containing the chart to delete. Find it in the URL: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/SPREADSHEET_ID/e

tools.name: Delete Dimension (Rows/Columns)
tools.description: Tool to delete specified rows or columns from a sheet in a Google Spreadsheet. Use when you need to remove a range of rows or columns.

inputs.name: sheet_id
inputs.about: The unique numeric ID of the sheet (not the index/position). This ID is assigned by Google Sheets and does not change when sheets are reordered. Use GOOGLESHEETS_GET_SPREADSHEET_INFO to find the sheet ID, or use sheet_name instead. Either sheet_id or sheet_name must be provided.

inputs.name: dimension
inputs.about: The dimension to delete (ROWS or COLUMNS).

inputs.name: end_index
inputs.about: The zero-based end index of the range to delete, exclusive. Must be greater than start_index and at most equal to the sheet's current row/column count. Note: Cannot delete all rows or columns from a sheet - at least one row and one column must remain.

inputs.name: sheet_name
inputs.about: The name/title of the sheet from which to delete the dimension. Using sheet_name is recommended as it's more intuitive than sheet_id. Either sheet_id or sheet_name must be provided.

inputs.name: start_index
inputs.about: The zero-based start index of the range to delete, inclusive. Must be less than end_index and within the sheet's current row/column count. Note: Cannot delete all rows or columns from a sheet - at least one row and one column must remain.

inputs.name: spreadsheet_id

inputs.name: response_ranges
inputs.about: Limits the ranges of cells included in the response spreadsheet.

inputs.name: delete_dimension_request
inputs.about: The details for the delete dimension request object.

inputs.name: response_include_grid_data
inputs.about: True if grid data should be returned. This parameter is ignored if a field mask was set in the request.

inputs.name: include_spreadsheet_in_response
inputs.about: Determines if the update response should include the spreadsheet resource.

tools.name: Delete Sheet
tools.description: Tool to delete a sheet (worksheet) from a spreadsheet. Use when you need to remove a specific sheet from a Google Sheet document.

inputs.name: sheetId
inputs.about: The ID of the sheet to delete. Note: A spreadsheet must contain at least one sheet, so you cannot delete the last remaining sheet. If the sheet is of DATA_SOURCE type, the associated DataSource is also deleted.

inputs.name: spreadsheetId
inputs.about: The ID of the spreadsheet from which to delete the sheet.

inputs.name: responseRanges
inputs.about: Limits which ranges are returned when includeSpreadsheetInResponse is true. Only meaningful if includeSpreadsheetInResponse is set to true. Ranges should be in A1 notation (e.g., 'Sheet1!A1:B10').

inputs.name: responseIncludeGridData
inputs.about: True if grid data should be returned in the response spreadsheet. Only meaningful when includeSpreadsheetInResponse is true and no field mask is set on the request.

inputs.name: includeSpreadsheetInResponse
inputs.about: Determines if the spreadsheet resource should be returned in the response. If true, the response includes the updated spreadsheet resource with all its sheets, properties, and metadata.

tools.description: Export an entire native spreadsheet as XLSX, ODS, PDF, ZIP, CSV, or TSV; use Export Sheet as PDF for print layout and range controls.

inputs.about: Opaque Drive file ID of a native Google Sheets spreadsheet, not its title or URL.

inputs.about: Official Drive export MIME type for spreadsheets: XLSX, ODS, PDF, zipped HTML, CSV, or TSV. CSV and TSV export only the first sheet.

tools.description: Render one sheet tab or rectangular range as PDF with orientation, gridline, margin, and fit-to-width controls.

inputs.name: bottom_margin

inputs.about: Sample-backed r2 range control. It must exceed start_row_index; Google does not formally document this browser-route key.

inputs.name: show_sheet_name

inputs.name: start_column_index

tools.description: Finds and replaces text across cells in a Google Spreadsheet, scoped to a sheet, range, or all sheets; if no scope is specified, it searches all sheets. Formula cells can be included explicitly when fixing formula references or patterns.

inputs.name: find
inputs.about: The text to find. Can be a literal string or a regular expression pattern.

inputs.about: The text to replace the found instances with.

inputs.about: Whether to search across all sheets in the spreadsheet. Mutually exclusive with sheet_id and range parameters.

inputs.name: matchCase
